study type: Mixed-methods (Ex vivo human tissue analysis and In vitro cell culture)
exposure: Co-culture with HTR-8/SVneo trophoblast cell line
IL-4/IL-13 induction of M2-like THP-1 macrophages
outcome: Decidual macrophage (dMph) polarization (M1 markers CD80, CD86; M2 markers CD163, CD206)
Granulocyte colony-stimulating factor receptor (G-CSFR) expression in placental trophoblasts
cohort: The study included human placental tissue from patients with Placenta Accreta (n=5) and controls (n=9), alongside human trophoblast (HTR-8/SVneo) and monocyte (THP-1) cell lines for in vitro experiments.
finding: Placenta Accreta is associated with an altered immune imbalance at the maternal-fetal interface, characterized by increased M2-like decidual macrophage polarization and higher G-CSFR expression in trophoblasts, with M2-like macrophages promoting trophoblast proliferation, invasion, and adhesion.
cross-section timing: Placental tissue samples were analyzed, presumably collected at the time of delivery.
